title: Observability: metrics + tracing for model changelog generator pipeline (publish lag, validation failures, docs sync failures)
author: Logan Wright
description:
Context: As we roll out the model changelog generator (registry change-events -> draft -> approval -> publish -> docs sync), we currently have a lot of "it seems stuck" reports with no quick answer for: (a) how far behind are we, (b) are we failing validation, (c) is docs sync failing vs generator failing, and (d) where are drafts piling up waiting for review.

This PR adds first-class metrics and tracing to the generator pipeline and wires them into Redwood dashboards/alerts. Goal is to make failures actionable (pager vs ticket), and make publish latency visible for the phased Console beta.

What’s included (high level):
- Prometheus metrics (counter/gauge/histogram) for each pipeline stage + error classes.
- Publish lag measurement from event timestamp -> published timestamp, plus per-stage latencies.
- Explicit docs publish/sync instrumentation (separate from generator render/store).
- OpenTelemetry spans + attributes for end-to-end correlation across: model-registry event ingest -> render -> approval state transitions -> docs publish job enqueue -> docs sync completion.
- Dashboard panels + alert rules (behind existing internal-only dashboards folder).

Notes:
- We intentionally do NOT label metrics with raw model_id/version_id to avoid high-cardinality blowups. We bucket by model_family and deployment_mode only (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Trace attributes include model_id/version_id/event_id, but sampled at 5% by default (configurable).

Follow-ups:
- Add an SLO doc for generator publish lag (proposal in ENG-4930 comments).
- Hook customer-visible status into Console (separate PR; Chloe tracking).

implementation_details:
Metrics added (Prometheus):
- redwood_changelog_generator_events_consumed_total{deployment_mode}
- redwood_changelog_generator_event_process_latency_seconds_bucket{stage, deployment_mode} (stages: ingest, render, validate, store_draft, approval_transition, publish, docs_enqueue, docs_sync)
- redwood_changelog_generator_publish_lag_seconds_bucket{deployment_mode} (event.created_at -> entry.published_at)
- redwood_changelog_generator_validation_failures_total{reason, deployment_mode} (reasons: missing_required_field, invalid_deprecation_window, incompatible_capability_flag, schema_version_unknown)
- redwood_changelog_generator_docs_sync_failures_total{reason} (reasons: 5xx, timeout, invalid_payload, not_found)
- redwood_changelog_generator_drafts_in_state{state} gauge (states: draft, in_review)
- redwood_changelog_generator_approvals_backlog_seconds{state} histogram (time in draft/in_review)

Tracing (OpenTelemetry):
- Span names: changelog.event.consume, changelog.render, changelog.validate, changelog.store_draft, changelog.publish, changelog.docs.enqueue, changelog.docs.sync
- Key attributes: event_id, change_type, schema_version, deployment_mode, model_id, version_id, approval_state (NOTE: model_id/version_id are trace-only; not metric labels)
- Context propagation: queue message now carries W3C traceparent + tracestate; worker extracts and continues span.

Dashboards/alerts:
- Dashboard: "Model Changelog Generator" panels for publish lag p50/p95, validation failure rate, docs sync errors, approvals backlog, and end-to-end throughput.
- Alerts (initial thresholds; will tune post-beta):
  - Publish lag p95 > 6h for 30m (ticket)
  - Publish lag p95 > 24h for 15m (page)
  - Validation failures > 10/min for 10m (ticket)
  - Docs sync failures > 2% of publish attempts for 10m (ticket)
  - Approvals backlog > 100 drafts in_review for 4h (ticket)

Illustrative snippet (metrics label policy):
We explicitly avoid raw model identifiers in metric labels:
- OK: deployment_mode=hosted, model_family=llama3
- NOT OK: model_id=meta/llama-3.1-70b-instruct, version_id=2026-02-18.1

Config:
- Added config knobs for trace sampling rate and docs sync timeout; defaults set conservatively for beta.
review_conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we confirm we’re not putting model_id/version_id into metric labels anywhere? I see attributes in tracing.go which is fine, but I want to make sure the histogram labels don’t accidentally include version_id when we call WithLabelValues.

Logan Wright (author): Yep. Metrics only label by deployment_mode + stage (+ reason for failures). Added a unit test in observability_test.go that asserts metric label sets match the allowlist and fails if version_id/model_id are used as labels.
Michael Nguyen (review): Publish lag definition: are we using registry event timestamp or the time we first saw the message? I’d prefer event.created_at so it captures upstream delays too.

Logan Wright (author): Using event.created_at (from registry event payload). Also recording ingest lag separately (now - message.enqueued_at) so we can tell backlog vs upstream. Updated naming in dashboard to make it clear.
Chloe Martin (review): For docs sync failures, can we differentiate docs enqueue failures (control plane -> docs job) vs docs callback handler failures?

Logan Wright (author): Added separate counters: docs_enqueue_failures_total and docs_sync_failures_total, plus per-stage latency buckets. Dashboard now shows both lines; alert uses the sync failure ratio because that’s what customers notice first.
Connor O'Brien (review): Any risk these alerts page during freeze windows when we intentionally pause publishes?

Logan Wright (author): Good point. Added an "publishing_enabled" gauge and an alert condition that requires publishing_enabled==1 for paging alerts. During freeze, we can flip config and still collect backlog metrics.
Allison Grant (final): Looks good with the label allowlist test + paging guard. Approving.
release_notes: Internal-only: Added monitoring for model changelog generator publish lag, validation failures, docs sync failures, and approval backlog; added distributed tracing for pipeline stages; added baseline dashboard + alerts for beta rollout.
